questions.q: Why can't you choose k by picking the value with the lowest inertia?
options: Inertia is not defined for k above 2
Inertia never changes when k changes
Lower inertia always means fewer clusters
Inertia keeps falling as k increases, reaching zero when every row is its own cluster
questions.explain: More centroids can only bring rows closer to a centroid, so inertia always decreases with k. You look for the point of diminishing returns instead.

questions.q: In the lesson's results, inertia went from 304.6 at k = 2 to 52.4 at k = 3, then to 42.3 at k = 4. What is the elbow?
options: k = 2, the largest inertia
k = 3, where the big drop ends and later improvements are small
k = 8, the lowest inertia
There is no elbow
questions.explain: The curve bends sharply at k = 3: a huge improvement to get there, and only small gains afterward.

questions.q: How do you use the silhouette score to choose k?
options: Choose the k with the lowest silhouette
Choose the k whose silhouette equals the number of clusters
Compare the mean silhouette across candidate values of k and prefer the highest
Average the silhouette over all values of k
questions.explain: Unlike inertia, silhouette can fall as k grows, so a peak (0.773 at k = 3 here) points to well-separated groups.

questions.q: Two values of k have almost identical silhouette scores. Which practical rule does the lesson suggest?
options: Always choose the larger k
Prefer the smaller k, since fewer segments are easier to explain and act on
Choose randomly
Discard the data
questions.explain: When metrics are close, simpler is better. Also profile the candidate clusters and check stability across seeds.

questions.q: Which is a good stability check for a clustering result?
options: Rerun k-means with different random seeds or on resampled data and see whether the groups stay similar
Confirm that inertia is above zero
Check that all clusters have exactly the same size
Make sure the cluster labels are 0, 1, 2 in order
questions.explain: If groups keep changing when you resample or reseed, they are probably not real structure.
